faq.q: Why is calm water like a mirror?
faq.a: A smooth water surface reflects light at the same angle it arrives, just like a mirror. So on a still day you see a clear reflection of the Sun, sky and trees.
asks: Why can I see reflections in a lake?

faq.a: A glitter path is the band of sparkles on rippled water stretching from you towards the Sun or Moon. Ripples along that line are the ones able to tilt sunlight into your eyes.
asks: Why is there a shiny path on the sea towards the Sun?
What is the line of light on water at sunset?

faq.a: Waves keep moving, so a ripple that was tilted just right a moment ago tilts away, and another one tilts into position. Each glint lasts only a split second.
asks: Why do glints turn on and off?

faq.q: Does everyone see the same glitter path?
faq.a: No. The path always points from your own eyes towards the Sun, so two friends standing apart see two different paths, each one seeming to follow them.
asks: Why does the path of light follow me?
Why does the moonlight path move with me?

faq.q: Why does the sea sparkle more when it is windy?
faq.a: More wind makes more ripples tilted at more angles, so the reflection spreads into a wide band of glints instead of one sharp image.
asks: Why does a rough sea glitter?
Why is a windy lake so sparkly?

facts: The band of glints on rippled water pointing towards the Sun or Moon is called a glitter path.
Calm water gives a single mirror-like image of the Sun; ripples break it into many separate glints.

quiz.say: Two friends stand 50 metres apart on a beach at sunset. Do they see the same glitter path on the sea?

options.show: Each a different path, pointing from them to the Sun
options.say: Each a different path, pointing from them to the Sun

quiz.why: The glitter path is made by ripples between each person and the Sun, so everyone sees their own path.

wrong.0: The path depends on where you stand, so it differs for each person.
wrong.2: As long as the sea is rippled and the Sun is visible, both see a path.
